clue.text: Delivery charge?

parts.note: read not as a postage fee but as the price paid to get a kidnapped person delivered back safely

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a courier's fee; the question mark signals that 'delivery' means the release of a hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper demands this sum as the price of freeing a captive, so it is literally a charge for delivery.

clue.text: Father in service with expedition

indicators.note: one word placed within the other

parts.note: an ace is an unreturned service in tennis
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A priest conducting a church service, accompanied by a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church, but here it is a tennis serve, ACE. 'with expedition' means speedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means quickly; expedition here is promptness or speed.

clue.text: Upheld when action taken about slur

indicators.note: the legal word goes around the word for slur

parts.note: sued means legal action was taken
a stain is a slur on one's reputation

explanation.surface: A court upholds a complaint once a defamation suit is brought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the legal word around the slur word; 'when' is a link. 'Upheld' fits a court sustaining a claim, matching the lawsuit surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained means supported or upheld, as when a judge sustains an objection.

clue.text: One study to hold up scholar's First?

indicators.note: in this down answer, the lower words support the scholar word from beneath

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
I is the Roman numeral one
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A student tries to support a classmate's first-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold up' in a down clue puts I and DEN underneath MA. The question mark marks First as a sense like a first voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden describes something done for the first time, as in a maiden voyage or maiden speech.

clue.text: Lozenge or gum taken without harm

indicators.note: the word for gum is placed outside, i.e. taken round, the word for harm

parts.note: paste is an adhesive, a gum for sticking paper
ill as a noun means harm or misfortune

explanation.surface: A choice between a throat sweet and chewing gum, either taken without any ill effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gum' suggests chewing gum, but here it is adhesive paste; 'taken without' wraps it around the harm word, and 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small medicated sweet sucked for a sore throat, the same thing as a lozenge.

clue.text: Trip to Reno no fun perhaps when things are irreversible

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible rearrangement of the preceding letters

explanation.surface: A trip to Nevada that turns out joyless is a stage you cannot undo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the fifteen letters of TRIP TO RENO NO FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names the stage at which turning back becomes impossible, so events cannot be reversed.

clue.text: Trace on position obtained by direction finder

parts.note: a sign is a trace or indication
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A navigator fixes a position using a direction-finding instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direction finder' suggests radio navigation, but a roadside pointer helps travellers find their way; 'on' and 'obtained by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost points travellers toward places, helping them find the right way.

clue.text: Gin cocktail to set up in the bar

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed
in a down answer, the word to is turned upwards, read backwards

explanation.surface: Mixing a gin cocktail to be served in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' makes ING from GIN and 'set up' turns TO into OT; 'in the bar' suggests a pub but 'bar' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, typically gold.

clue.text: Occupation offering money with comfort and influence

parts.note: L stands for pound, a unit of money
ease means comfort
a hold is power or influence over someone

explanation.surface: A job that brings wealth, comfort and power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' suggests a job but means occupancy of property.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold is tenure of property under a lease, a form of occupancy of land.

clue.text: Suffered illness, having imbibed Scotch at the start of merrymaking

indicators.note: drinking something in, so the phrase for being ill swallows a letter

parts.note: was ailing means suffered an illness

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Scotch is used

explanation.surface: Someone fell ill after drinking whisky at the beginning of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having imbibed' puts S (the start of Scotch) inside WAS AILING. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing is old-fashioned festive drinking and carousing, a form of merrymaking.

clue.text: Prompt to leave, given notice

parts.note: to go is to leave
an ad, advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: An employee is pushed to quit after being handed their notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad someone is to spur or urge them into action, i.e. to prompt them.

clue.text: Dissolute rebel imprisoned in nick

indicators.note: locked up inside, so one word is set within the other

parts.note: a dent is a small nick or notch
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A dissipated rebel is locked up in a police cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' suggests a prison (British slang), but here it is a notch, DENT. Jack CADE was an English rebel of 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes someone self-indulgent and morally lax, much like dissolute.

clue.text: Speak softly at first in club

indicators.note: the soft marking comes before the speaking word, at the front

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for softly
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: Advice to talk quietly at first when in a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' places P before UTTER although the clue gives them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used on the green for short strokes toward the hole.

clue.text: Painting from Romantic once popular

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A picture by a Romantic artist that was once in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'romantIC ONce'; 'popular' completes the surface and also nods to the word's sense of a celebrated figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a religious image painted on wood, especially in the Orthodox church.

clue.text: Escort for dictator in each turnout

indicators.note: one item placed inside another
turned out letters are rearranged

parts.note: Juan Perón was Argentina's authoritarian leader

explanation.surface: A bodyguard for a tyrant at each public appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnout' rearranges EACH into CHAE, and 'in' sets the Argentine leader inside. Perón ruled Argentina in the 1940s and 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies and supervises a young person, acting as an escort.

clue.text: Is such grub served only during Lent?

definitions.text: Is such grub served only during Lent?

parts.words: Is such grub served only during Lent?
parts.note: plays on the quick burgers-and-chips sense against food eaten while fasting, as in the Lenten season

explanation.walkthrough: Lent is the Christian season of fasting; the clue reads 'fast' as abstaining from food rather than as quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick takeaway meals like burgers are called this; the clue twists 'fast' to mean abstaining from eating.

clue.text: Functions in support of launch of scintillating show

indicators.note: in a down answer, the functions word sits beneath, supporting the launch word

parts.note: to fire is to launch, as a rocket
works means functions, operates

explanation.surface: Ceremonies held to support a product launch with a dazzling display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in support of' places WORKS below FIRE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireworks display is a sparkling show of pyrotechnics.

clue.text: Brings to fruition from twigs

definitions.meaning: British informal verb for grasps or understands

explanation.surface: Something growing fruit from its branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twigs' looks like branches but is the verb meaning understands; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Realises means makes real or achieves, and also understands, which is what 'twigs' means informally.

clue.text: Diagnose injury in America

indicators.note: injured letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor identifies an injury in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injury' signals rearranging DIAGNOSE. The definition 'in America' stands for a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large Californian city, a place located in America.

clue.text: Travelled on right lines

parts.note: an ode is a poem, i.e. lines of verse

explanation.surface: Someone journeyed along the correct railway lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like rails but means lines of poetry; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, so it means went on a journey by horse or vehicle.

clue.text: Stood by and helped to enthrone Bishop

indicators.note: to seat within, so the bishop letter is set inside the helping word

parts.note: aided means helped
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone loyally helped at a bishop's enthronement ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enthrone' puts B inside AIDED; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abided means stayed loyal or kept to, so stood by a decision or person.

clue.text: Animal with wide support

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
an easel is a stand supporting a painting

explanation.surface: A creature with a broad base to stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: The weasel is a small slender carnivorous mammal.

clue.text: Writer in a way is exhausted

indicators.note: the writing word goes inside the way word

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author is worn out in some respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as 'somewhat' but gives PEN in ST; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, tired out, completely drained.

clue.text: Bridge player in debt about a pound needs nudging

parts.note: East, E, is one of the four seats at the bridge table
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
owing means in debt

explanation.surface: A card player who owes about a pound has to keep jogging others.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge seats are North, South, East and West, so any of N, S, E, W can be a 'bridge player'; 'about' and 'needs' are only surface and link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbowing means pushing with the elbow, a jostling, prodding action like nudging.

clue.text: Opening for husband in pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: the pleasant word surrounds the husband letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A vacancy for a married man in an attractive setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' puts NICE around H; 'for' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or gap, an opening, as in a niche in the market.

clue.text: Re-styled shoe or stockings, say

indicators.note: something re-styled is reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restyled footwear, or perhaps hosiery, at a fashion shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-styled' rearranges SHOE; 'say' marks stockings as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is a collective term for legwear such as tights and stockings, which are one example.

clue.text: Perfect course on which to set a record

definitions.text: on which to set a record

parts.note: sound means whole or in perfect condition
a track is a course, as in a racecourse

explanation.surface: An ideal racetrack where an athlete might break a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set a record' suggests athletics; the definition means recording music onto a film's audio strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's soundtrack is the strip where its audio is recorded, so a record is set on it.

clue.text: Sit back at rear of aircraft about to ditch

indicators.note: the reversed sitting word goes behind the aircraft word

parts.note: a jet is a type of aircraft

indicators.note: the word sit is read backwards

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone sits at the back of a plane that is about to crash into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SIT into TIS and 'at rear of' places it behind the aircraft; 'to' is a link. 'ditch' as a verb means discard, not a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw cargo overboard or discard it, to ditch it.

clue.text: Eliminate mince pies in extremely doubtful wrapping

indicators.note: the outer letters are wrapped around the rearranged letters
only the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word doubtful
to mince is to chop up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting rid of suspect mince pies in dubious packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' turns PIES into ISPE; 'extremely' takes D and L, the first and last letters of 'doubtful', and 'wrapping' puts them around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or banish, i.e. to eliminate doubts or fears.
